rules.title: Prohibition on Algorithmic Rent-Setting Software
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use software that pools nonpublic data from two or more landlords to set, recommend, or adjust rents or occupancy levels for units in covered buildings (6+ residential rental units). No person may sell, license, or provide such software to landlords to set rents for units in the City. Violations carry civil fines of up to $1,000 each, and tenants may sue.
rules.key_value: Prohibited in buildings with 6+ rental units; fine up to $1,000 per violation
rules.quoted_span:
(a) No landlord shall use algorithmic rent-setting software to set, recommend, or adjust
the rent or occupancy level of any residential rental unit in a covered building.

enacted_date.quoted_span: Adopted by the City Council of the City of Cambridge on September 14, 2026.

effective_dates.raw: one hundred eighty (180) days after its adoption
effective_dates.quoted_span: This ordinance shall take effect one hundred eighty (180) days after its adoption.

exemption_conditions.condition: Buildings containing fewer than six residential rental units are exempt.
Units owned or operated by the Cambridge Housing Authority are exempt.

coverage.notes: Subsection (b) bars any person from selling, licensing, or providing such software to a landlord for setting rents on residential rental units in the City, without referring to covered buildings.

rules.coverage_text: Landlords (owners, lessors, sublessors, and their agents) of residential rental units in covered buildings, meaning buildings in Cambridge with six or more residential rental units. Also covers any person who provides algorithmic rent-setting software to landlords for units in the City.
rules.exemptions: Buildings with fewer than six residential rental units; units owned or operated by the Cambridge Housing Authority.
